paraphrase: The eighteen Purāṇas are Brāhma, Pādma, Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, Bhāgavata, Bhaviṣya, Nāradīya, Mārkaṇḍeya, Āgneya, Brahmavaivarta, Laiṅga, Vārāha, Skānda, Vāmana, Kaurma, Mātsya, Gāruḍa and then the Vāyavīya - the eighteenth, called Brahmāṇḍa; the Upapurāṇas told by sages are: first the Sanatkumāra, then the Nārasiṃha, the Skānda spoken by Kumāra, the Śivadharma spoken by Nandīśa, the Āścarya spoken by Durvāsas, the Nāradīya, Kāpila, Mānava, Auśanasa, Brahmāṇḍa, Vāruṇa, Kālikā, Māheśvara, Sāmba, Saura, the one spoken by Parāśara, the Mārīca and the Bhārgava.

paraphrase: [At the end of the story of the skull-bearing Lord freed from the sin of brahmin-murder at the holy tīrtha] Śiva says: the sin of those who constantly remember my excellent skull-bearer's guise quickly perishes, here and hereafter; whoever comes to this best of tīrthas, bathes and offers to ancestors and gods is freed from brahmin-murder.
speaker: Śiva

paraphrase: Śiva tells the sages of the pine forest: calm, self-controlled, smeared with ash, celibate and naked one should keep the Pāśupata vow; I made the supreme Pāśupata vow long ago, most secret, the essence of the Veda, for liberation; or, wearing a loincloth or single garment, devoted to Vedic study, one should meditate on Paśupati Śiva - this Pāśupata yoga is to be followed by seekers of release. Other scriptures contrary to the Veda I taught for delusion: the Vāma, Pāśupata, Soma, Lākula and Bhairava are declared not to be followed, being outside the Veda.
